title: Count and list the long words from one stream supplier

blocks.text: A stream is **single-use**: once a terminal operation has consumed it, using it again throws `IllegalStateException`. When the same pipeline must answer two questions, the fix is a new stream for each terminal operation, and a `Supplier<Stream<T>>` is a tidy way to hand them out.

items: `longerThan(List<String> words, int min)` returns a `Supplier<Stream<String>>` whose every `get()` yields a stream of the words longer than `min` characters, in their order.

`report(List<String> words, int min)` returns a `LongWords.Report(long count, List<String> words)` holding how many words are longer than `min` and the words themselves (a word that repeats counts, and is listed, each time). The supplier of method 1 is a natural way to get both parts.

blocks.text: A caller may call `get()` as often as it likes. Mind the word that is exactly `min` long.

cases.says: The report carries how many words are longer than the minimum, and which.
Every get() on the supplier returns a new stream: a stream consumed once cannot be used again.
A word whose length equals the minimum is not longer than it.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A stream is single-use, so each terminal operation needs a fresh stream from the source.
